drafts.title: Let drivers view, export and delete their driver profile data from vehicle or account
drafts.description: Customers can inspect what data the vehicle stores in their driver profile, export a copy, and permanently delete the profile (local + cloud) without contacting BMW support.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A driver can (1) view a summary of stored profile fields, (2) export the full profile to a common format (e.g. JSON) and receive a download link within 2 minutes, and (3) delete the profile and receive confirmation; deletion propagates to cloud and local vehicle storage within 24 hours in 95% of test cases.
assumptions: Vehicle can communicate with BMW cloud for profile sync under typical network conditions (4G/5G/Wi‑Fi) or provide an equivalent local-only flow.
Export and deletion semantics (which fields are included) will be defined by product policy prior to launch.
uncertainties: Exact fields customers expect to see/export/delete may vary by market and will require UX validation.
Time to propagate deletions may depend on cloud processing loads and will need monitoring.

drafts.title: Voice control reliably understands common driving commands
drafts.description: While driving, the voice assistant recognizes and executes common commands (navigation, climate, media, phone) with minimal frustration and without needing repeated phrasing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In vehicle driving tests with typical cabin noise, the system correctly interprets 95% of a curated set of 120 common driving commands across navigation, climate, media and phone tasks on first attempt.
assumptions: Training data for recognition includes common accents and cabin noise typical in the US market.
A curated test set of 120 representative commands will be agreed prior to evaluation.
uncertainties: Performance may vary for rare accents or non-standard phrasing; scope focuses on common commands.
Network-dependent features (cloud ASR) may have different latency/accuracy than onboard ASR.

drafts.title: Wireless charging pad reliably maintains charge for common phones during drives
drafts.description: The wireless charging pad keeps compatible phones charging without frequent dropouts during normal use and driving conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Across a test matrix of 12 popular phone models and common case thicknesses, the pad maintains an uninterrupted charging connection for 95% of 30-minute drives over a variety of cabin temperatures (0–35°C) and typical road vibrations.
assumptions: Phones tested follow the Qi charging standard and include typical case thicknesses up to 3 mm.
The test set of 12 phone models will represent >80% of US market share at launch.
uncertainties: Exotic phone models, magnetic accessories (e.g., MagSafe) or very thick cases may still cause drops.
Physical alignment behaviors by users (how they place the phone) will affect results.

drafts.title: Head‑up display remains legible in direct sunlight
drafts.description: Customers can read critical HUD content (speed, navigation arrows, alerts) even in bright sunlight without needing to lower a sun visor or change seating.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a standardized sunlight simulator at direct-sun levels (up to 80,000 lux), 90% of test participants can correctly read HUD speed and next-turn navigation information from the driver's normal seating position with glasses or sunglasses.
assumptions: Usability tests use a representative sample of users including sunglass wearers and typical seating positions.
Lighting test setup follows an agreed industry-standard method to simulate direct sunlight.
uncertainties: Extreme viewing angles, aftermarket windscreen films or heavily polarized sunglasses may reduce legibility.
Acceptable trade-offs between HUD brightness and night-time glare will need validation.

drafts.title: Physical climate controls that can be operated without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can change temperature and fan speed by feel using dedicated physical controls so they do not need to look at the screen while driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In on-road usability tests, 95% of participants can locate and adjust cabin temperature by +/−2°C and increase/decrease fan speed by one level within 2 seconds without glancing at the center display.
assumptions: Controls are tactilely distinct and placed within the driver's muscle memory reach.
Usability testing includes drivers of a range of hand sizes and driving postures.
uncertainties: Exact control layout that balances clean interior design and tactile discoverability will need iterative UX testing.
Some premium trims may choose different control philosophies; target applies to at least base and popular trims.

drafts.title: Center screen readability improved to reduce glare in bright conditions
drafts.description: Customers can read and interact with the center screen in bright daylight with minimal reflections or washed-out contrast.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In standardized bright-light tests (up to 80,000 lux) at typical driver viewing angles, 85% of participants can read common UI elements (menu labels, navigation text) on the center screen without repositioning or shading.
assumptions: Tests use a representative set of UI screens and font sizes used in production.
Anti-reflective coatings and screen angle adjustments are considered as solutions.
uncertainties: Extreme sun angles through panoramic roofs or aftermarket window tints may still cause visibility issues.
Trade-offs between screen brightness, power consumption and night-time comfort will need optimization.

drafts.title: Include heated steering wheel as part of the cold‑weather package
drafts.description: Customers who order the cold‑weather (winter) package receive a heated steering wheel as a bundled feature so it is not sold separately by default.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In US market configuration, the cold‑weather package must include the heated steering wheel as a standard item for at least one commonly ordered trim; configuration data confirms inclusion at launch.
assumptions: Product catalog and dealer configurator will be updated to reflect packaging and SKU changes before launch.
Market-specific package contents can differ; this requirement targets the US market.
uncertainties: Exact trim(s) where package is standard may be decided by regional product planning.
Customer perception of value versus price will need monitoring (pricing is handled separately).

drafts.title: CCC certification request for Chinese market (out of scope: certification/regulation)
drafts.description: Customers request that the infotainment system passes CCC certification for sale in China.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: This request is a certification/regulatory requirement and is out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Certification and homologation (CCC) are regulatory tasks, not customer-facing feature definitions; handled in compliance/homologation track.

drafts.title: Request for a specific cockpit chip (Snapdragon 8295) (out of scope: engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the cockpit computer use the Snapdragon 8295 chip.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request for a specific semiconductor is an engineering specification and out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Component-level requests (specific chip models) are engineering specifications and not customer-facing outcomes.

drafts.title: Requests about base price, leasing, subscription price and dealer margins (out of scope: price/finance/business case)
drafts.description: Customers asked for a lower base price, cheaper lease, free packages, discounts on the Comfort package, lower dealer margins, a $15/month heated seat subscription, cheaper heated-steering-wheel option, and 0% financing.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Pricing, financing and dealer margin requests are business/pricing topics and are out of scope for product functional requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Price, subscription pricing, financing and dealer margin are business and commercial decisions outside the scope of customer-facing product requirements.
